report.verdict: A financial analyst’s resume aimed at a marketing operations role that asks for different experience and tools.
write_up: This marketing operations job is a different track from your finance experience. I read your resume for Financial Analyst roles: your corporate FP&A and banking work give a recruiter a clear reason to move it forward, with a few questions about how you achieved your results.

The headcount model line is your best model. It names Adaptive Planning, what you rebuilt and the spreadsheets it replaced. Your most prominent figures are strong, but they leave out the work behind them.

Start with the savings and forecast lines at Piedmont. Add the method and the part of the business involved, then do the same for reporting efficiency and month-end automation. For Tallgrass, bring forward any real campaign work you can substantiate; finance reporting alone doesn't establish marketing operations experience.

cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see the amount, but not where you found it or how. Those details would show the finance work behind the figure.
cards.question: Where did you identify the savings, and how did you find them?

cards.cannot_tell: The improvement is concrete, but the forecast and your approach aren't named. A recruiter will want to know what you changed.

cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model: it gives the recruiter a named deliverable and shows what was in place before your work.

fit.why: Your headline and both jobs point to financial analysis, including FP&A, forecasting and branch profitability reporting.
fit.level: mid-level, current corporate FP&A role and an earlier Financial Analyst role
fit.note: Your reporting and dashboard tools give you a foundation relevant to the reporting side of Tallgrass's work. If you have campaign or marketing systems experience, add only the work you can substantiate.

posting.summary: Tallgrass wants a marketing operations coordinator to run campaigns, maintain lead data, report on performance and support events.
